page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core, which eliminates hyperthreading overhead. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate solid multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,571.1 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,706.0, both falling within the average range. Single-core performance is comparatively weaker, as seen in the Geekbench single-core score of 958.0 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression rate of 20.31 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 1,894.03 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 173.34 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage combined with dedicated ARM cores makes this instance highly suitable for workloads requiring local scratch space, such as software compilation and database operations. It also handles static web serving efficiently, achieving 33.11 GB/sec in throughput tests. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture offers a resource-dense compute profile with a lower power footprint compared to traditional x86 architectures, though single-threaded tasks represent a performance tradeoff.
